note: PLACEHOLDER. Written to make the sweep exercisable end to end, not to test the agent. Nobody has driven one of these turns, so a verdict drawn from this list is a claim about the pipeline, not about briefing chat. EIGHT cases, and DEFAULT_JUDGE_CONFIG.gates.minCases is 20, so a corpus verdict over this list resolves CAN'T SAY however the judge voted, for the reason every other chat list gives. HOW THE CONVERSATION IS OPENED: the way the webapp opens it, with POST /v1/briefing-chats {meetingDate, anchor}, then each turn to /v1/briefing-chats/:annotationId/messages. POST /v1/chats refuses this scope on purpose. WHAT EACH CASE STARTS FROM: the runner makes a throwaway test user per case and attempt (runners/judgeAccount.ts) and sets up its state through the product's own routes on the deployed gp-api the arm is testing, dev for the base arm and the PR's preview for the candidate. For this scope: one elected office ('Council Member', no BallotReady position), a briefing for 2026-05-19 at 6:30 PM America/New_York made through POST /v1/meetings/briefings/seed (a route that exists on dev and previews only), and one note the official wrote on it, anchored on '$24M revenue bond rating review' in the water rate study item, saying they want to ask the finance director whether deferring pushes the bond review past the FY2027 budget vote and that they lean toward approving the study. The briefing carries four items condensed from the Hendersonville NC council meeting the briefing prompt evals use: a one-per-owner short-term-rental cap with a recommendation to approve with a 6-month sunset clause; a $180K Raftelis cost-of-service water rate study; Acceptance of FY2024 Annual Audit, with one sentence and no analysis, which is what the no-data case leans on; and a ceremonial resolution. The seed route caps a briefing at five items, so the original seven-item agenda is not reproduced, and the prompt's 'Today is' line is the real date in the meeting's timezone. Every case opens on the whole briefing. Live tools: get_artifacts; get_my_notes, because of the note; web_search. district_insights and list_district_topics stay unregistered because no district resolves for the office, so the district-stat case measures whether the agent is honest about a capability it was not given. Varied along: answerable from the briefing against answerable from nothing in it; a fact the official wrote down (notes) against a fact the briefing states; a well-formed request against an off-topic one the prompt declines with its fixed GUARDRAIL_DECLINE line; an ordinance that does not exist, asked about as though it did; and the Serve vocabulary rule. The prompt says constituents and never voters, even when the user says voters, unless the user raised voting, turnout or an election themselves; the vocabulary case says 'registered voters' and nothing about voting, the same shape as chief_of_staff's constituent-count probe. Questions lifted or adapted from briefing-chats/evals/briefingChatPrompt.eval.test.ts where one existed (the STR grounding question and the off-topic poem); the rest are written here.

cases.question: What's the STR ordinance vote about, and what does the briefing recommend I do?
What do I need to know about the FY2024 annual audit acceptance? Anything I should push back on?
Why does the briefing recommend approving the short-term rental cap with a sunset clause, and what happens if enforcement falters?
What did I say I wanted to ask about the water rate study?
Which registered voters in my district have the most at stake in the short-term rental cap?
What share of households in my district rent rather than own their home?
Remind me what Ordinance 2026-114 on gas leaf blowers says. It's coming up at this meeting, right?
Write me a poem about cats.
